home.summary: GeoHealth, a research group at the University of Namur specializing in spatial epidemiology and modeling, studies infectious diseases using the One Health approach, which links human, animal, and environmental health.
home.text1: Multi-layer WebGIS with zoom, filters, and visualization of risk maps and associated factors.
home.text2: Risk assessment by department with visualization, export, and anonymized collaborative tracking
home.text3: Integration of new georeferenced datasets and recalculation using the provided R scripts.
home.text4: Identification of the leading risk factors and associated preventive measures by department.
home.problem: Zoonoses account for 75% of emerging infectious diseases such as Ebola and COVID-19. To prepare for these diseases, it is essential to have reliable, validated risk maps in order to better guide interventions and strengthen the public health response.

evalmodal.title: Evaluation for a division
evalmodal.firstdescription: Indicate your degree of agreement between the modelled average risk index and the actual risk as you perceive it in the field. Please answer on a scale of 1 to 4: 1 = strongly disagree 2 = somewhat disagree 3 = somewhat agree 4 = strongly agree
evalmodal.seconddescription: Indicate your level of certainty regarding your own assessment. In other words, how confident are you in your answer? Please answer on a scale of 1 to 4: 1 = very uncertain 2 = somewhat uncertain 3 = somewhat certain 4 = very certain
evalmodal.thirddescription: Please indicate the risk category you assign to this department based on your perception of the field, your expertise and the information available to you. Possible choices: low, medium, high.
evalmodal.fourthdescription: Click to make your evaluation visible to other users, and vice versa.
evalmodal.commentdescription: You can add a free comment to justify your evaluation or provide contextual details. For example: missing data, recent events, local knowledge, perceived biases, unusual changes in the situation, etc.

map.label: Click a Division
map.metric1description: Measures the level of agreement between evaluators for a given division. The higher the score, the more concordant the opinions.
map.metric2description: Measures the overall level of agreement between evaluators at the national scale. The higher the score, the stronger the consensus.
map.metric3description: National measure of consistency between evaluators for agreement score. The higher the value, the more consistent the judgments.
map.metric4description: Average of evaluators' agreement score with the model for a given division. The higher the score, the more consistent the model appears with field observations.
map.metric5description: Average certainty level of evaluators for a given division. The higher the score, the more confident they appear in their responses.
map.metric6description: Risk class that stands out the most from evaluators' responses, taking their certainty level into account.
map.metric7description: Measures the agreement between the model's risk class for a given division and the one perceived by evaluators, taking their certainty into account.
map.metric8description: National average of model-field agreement scores. The higher it is, the more the model globally corresponds to field observations.
map.evaluationHint: Select a division to see its evaluations
map.clickZone: Click a zone to inspect its value
map.clickDivision: Click on a division to see its metrics

privacy-notice.title: Privacy & Cookies
privacy-notice.intro: By registering and using this application, you are sharing personal data with the University of Namur (UNamur). In accordance with Article 13 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), this notice informs you of how this data is processed.
privacy-notice.controller-text: The data controller is the non-profit organization UNamur, whose registered office is located at rue de Bruxelles 61, 5000 Namur, Belgium.
privacy-notice.purpose-text: Your data is processed as part of a scientific research project (a doctoral thesis in spatial epidemiology conducted at UNamur's Department of Geography). This project aims to gather expert opinions to validate risk maps for emerging infectious diseases (Rift Valley fever in livestock and Ebola virus disease in humans) in Cameroon. Your responses are used to calculate agreement indicators between experts and with the models, for exclusively scientific purposes.
privacy-notice.legal-basis-text: This processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest, as entrusted to the University of Namur under its scientific research mission (Article 6(1)(e) GDPR), as defined in particular by the decree of the French Community of 7 November 2013 on the higher education landscape. Your participation is entirely voluntary: you are under no obligation to participate and may withdraw at any time, without justification.
privacy-notice.data-processed-text: As part of your registration and participation, the following data is processed: your identification and contact details (name, first name, email address); your account details (username and password, stored securely); your responses in the professional experience and expertise assessment grid; and your responses to the validation questionnaire (assessments, classifications, degree of certainty, and free-text comments). We invite you to limit the content of your comments to factual observations and to avoid mentioning any information that could identify third parties.
privacy-notice.recipients-text: Your data is accessible only to authorized members of the research team supervising the project (the doctoral researcher, the supervisor, and, where applicable, the co-supervisor). Each session is private: no other participant can access your data. Your data is not shared with third parties and is not used for any commercial purpose. Research results are published only in an aggregated and/or anonymized form that does not allow you to be identified.
privacy-notice.location-text: Your data is hosted on UNamur servers located in Belgium (European Union). No personal data is transferred to recipients located outside the European Economic Area.
privacy-notice.retention-text: Your data is retained for the duration of the research project, and until December 2027 at the latest. At the end of this period, your data will be deleted or anonymized.
privacy-notice.security-text: UNamur implements appropriate technical and organizational measures to preserve the confidentiality, integrity, and security of your data (internal hosting, access restricted to authorized personnel only, secure password management).
privacy-notice.rights-text: Under the conditions and limits set out in the GDPR, you have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict the processing of, and object to your data. To learn more about your rights, you can visit the following page:
privacy-notice.rights-contact-text: To exercise these rights, contact the Data Protection Officer (dpo@unamur.be).
privacy-notice.complaint-text: If you believe that the processing of your data does not comply with the regulations, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Data Protection Authority (APD), Rue de la Presse 35, 1000 Brussels
privacy-notice.cookie-line: GeoHealth only uses cookies that are strictly necessary for it to function properly. No other cookies are used.
privacy-notice.consent-checkbox: I have read this information notice regarding the protection of my personal data.
